To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the acclimation of sperm of the euryhaline fish tilapia Oreochomis mossambicus is associated with a shift of the source of increasing intracellular Ca2+, from intracellular stores to extracellular stores, and a shift of the site of protein phosphorylation, from cytoplasmic to axoneme.

the motility apparatus of sperm from freshwater-acclimated and seawater-acclinated tilapia are different, with the latter being activated by Ca2+ in hypertonic conditions and the former by intracellular Ca2+.
acclimation to seawater increases the sensitivity of sperm motility to extracellular Ca2+.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the acclimation of sperm in tilapia.
the mechanism underlying regulation of sperm motility in euryhaline fish, and the results provide a new insight into how sperm motility can be regulated in a hypertonic medium.
the acclimation of tilapia to different salinities.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the sperm motility apparatus is modulated by acclimation to different salinities.
the motility apparatus of SWT sperm is more resistant to hypertonic conditions than that of FWT sperm, and that SWT sperm are more resistant to osmotic stress than FWT sperm.
sperm motility apparatus is acclimatized during seawater acclimation in euryhaline fish, tilapia.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
acclimation is associated with the modulation of the flow and source of Ca2+ and phosphorylation of proteins associated with the motility apparatus in the euryhaline fish, tilapia.
the acclimation of sperm of tilapia to seawater is associated with modulation in sperm motility apparatus, which is regulated by extracellular Ca2+.

acclimation to seawater induces a change in the regulation of motility in tilapia sperm from intracellular to extracellular sources, and the change in the regulation appears to be associated with a modification of the motility activation system, such as Ca2+ and protein phosphorylation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the motility apparatus of SWT sperm is acclimated to seawater conditions.
the motility apparatus of tilapia sperm is acclimated to the osmotic environment.
the regulation of sperm motility in tilapia appears to be acclimated to the environment in which the fish are acclimated.
